triples.head: cell cycle
triples.evidence: Interphase includes the G1, S, and G2 phases.

triples.head: S phase
triples.evidence: During the S phase, DNA is replicated so each chromosome consists of two sister chromatids.

triples.head: S phase

triples.head: mitosis
triples.evidence: In prophase, chromosomes condense and the spindle begins to form. In metaphase, chromosomes line up at the cell's equator. In anaphase, sister chromatids separate and move to opposite poles. In telophase, nuclear envelopes reform around the separated chromosomes.

triples.head: cytokinesis
triples.evidence: Cytokinesis usually follows mitosis and divides the cytoplasm into two daughter cells.
